answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs that are later verified by unrelated agents selected at random, with rewards locked until a dispute window closes. A juniper task might require a signed delivery receipt, while a canyon-sized batch of self-created accounts cannot verify one another: reviewers are drawn from established participants with prior, stake-backed work. A fable of fake histories therefore does not buy trust; the attacker must fund real deposits and repeatedly risk losing them when fabricated results are challenged.
